items.title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — first Fable price cut (-20%), 30% faster output, takes #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5; Claude Code v2.1.321 follows the next day to make Fable 5.2 the default
items.summary: On November 9, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and a restricted sibling, Claude Mythos 5.2. Fable 5.2 is available on paid Claude plans, the API, and several cloud platforms; Mythos 5.2 is held back for vetted organizations with higher-capability access. Fable 5.2 list pricing is reported at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output — a ~20% reduction from Fable 5.1 and the first price cut in the Fable line. Anthropic says output is up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1. Artificial Analysis reportedly placed Fable 5.2 at #1 on its Intelligence Index v5 with a score of 65. Coverage emphasizes coding and technical work, and Anthropic cited an internal statistic that approximately 90% of its code is now written by Claude models. The next day, November 10, Claude Code v2.1.321 shipped and made Fable 5.2 the default model for the CLI, alongside a set of permission and MCP-secret handling fixes.
items.why_it_matters: This is the most consequential model release of the week and it slots directly into the AI-coding workflow Gabe already uses. Three threads worth noticing. First, the price cut is the real headline. Fable 5.2 landing at $8/$40 per million tokens — down from $10/$50 on 5.1 — is the first time Anthropic has dropped prices on its flagship Fable line, and it arrives one week before the IPO prices. Read that sequencing as a deliberate signal: Anthropic is telling the market that the unit economics are strong enough to absorb a price cut on their highest-margin product while revenue still grows at the 47% QoQ clip the S-1/A filing reported. For anyone running a hobby project on Claude's API, a 20% drop on the flagship is immediate and meaningful — the same monthly budget now covers more completions. Second, the #1 position on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at 65 matters because AA is the most-cited independent benchmarking source in the public discourse. Anthropic now leads the composite index ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon in the same window those two labs are also shipping updates — the gap at the top has closed to the point where it can flip on a single release, which is new. For Gabe's Python work, the practical read is that Claude Fable 5.2 is now plausibly the single strongest coding model available, so it is worth updating any local Claude CLI, API client, or agent wrapper to default to it. Third, the Claude Code v2.1.321 release the next day is the operational piece. Anthropic shipped the CLI update that makes Fable 5.2 the default within 24 hours of the model launch — a tight integration cycle that suggests they want developers moved onto the new model quickly. Running `claude --version` to confirm you are on 2.1.321 or later is the one practical step worth taking today. The Mythos 5.2 half of the release — gated to vetted organizations and not generally available — is the signal to watch separately: it is the capability ceiling Anthropic is comfortable showing partners but not the public, and historically the gap between Mythos and Fable shrinks over subsequent months as safety work completes. Expect Mythos 5.2 capabilities to reach Fable sometime in Q1 2027.
items.why_it_matters_brief: First price cut on the Fable line (-20%), 30% faster, and #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 — Anthropic shipped the strongest coding model available days before pricing the IPO.

items.title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview on Qianfan — first post-trained checkpoint of the 280B/14B-active open MoE Base released Nov 5; open-source weights promised before November 25
items.summary: On November 11, 2026, Baidu released ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview through its Qianfan platform. The Preview is the first post-trained checkpoint built on top of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, which Baidu released on November 5 as an open-weights text-only Mixture-of-Experts model with 280 billion total parameters and 14 billion activated per token. The Base checkpoint ships under a custom license, the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base Model License Agreement v1.0, which reportedly restricts commercial use by geography and by company revenue thresholds — read the license text before any production use. Baidu has said the Preview's open-source weights will be released before November 25. The API is available on Qianfan now. Coverage is almost entirely Chinese-language and secondary English translations; Baidu has not published English-language model-card documentation at the Preview tier yet.
items.why_it_matters: ERNIE 5.5 Flash is the second major open-weights release from a Chinese lab in three weeks — Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on October 23, and Baidu's drop follows the same playbook: large MoE (280B total, 14B active for ERNIE Flash vs. 2.8T/104B for Kimi K3.1 Pro), aggressive pricing, and a restrictive commercial license that gates downstream enterprise use. Three threads worth paying attention to. First, the architecture choice. A 280B MoE with 14B active parameters per token is the same shape as Mistral's Medium 3.5 and DeepSeek's V3 family — the active-parameter count is what determines inference cost, so a 14B-active model runs at a cost roughly comparable to a 14B dense model while retaining the capability profile of something much larger. For a Python developer running local inference (or renting time on a Hugging Face Inference Endpoint), that is the right sweet spot for a hobby budget. A 280B-total model also fits on a single H200 node once quantized to 4-bit, which is the current practical threshold for self-hosting outside a corporate environment. Second, the license is the catch. The ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base license reportedly restricts use by region and by company revenue — meaning the open-weights release is effectively a two-tier system where non-commercial hobby use is permitted but commercial deployment above revenue thresholds requires separate licensing. This is becoming the standard pattern for Chinese open-weights releases (Qwen, Kimi K3.1 Pro, and now ERNIE Flash all use custom licenses rather than Apache or MIT), and it is worth understanding as a category — true Apache 2.0 open-source releases from frontier labs are now the exception, not the rule. Third, the release cadence is a signal about the Chinese AI-lab IPO cycle. Baidu is publicly listed already but Moonshot is filing for a Hong Kong listing at a ~$50B valuation (noted in the am section this morning), and the pattern of 'drop open weights, then file for public listing' is clearly becoming the preferred path for Chinese labs to establish technical credibility before capital raises. For Gabe's HTML/CSS/Python stack, the practical near-term take is: watch for the open-source weights drop before Nov 25, try the Qianfan API now if a Baidu account is accessible, and treat this as evidence that the open-weights frontier is now reliably two to three weeks behind the proprietary frontier — Fable 5.2 landed Nov 9, ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview on Nov 11, and the public weights follow on a two-week lag.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Second large open-weights MoE from a Chinese lab in three weeks (280B total / 14B active) — the open-weights frontier is now two to three weeks behind the proprietary one, with a restrictive license as the standard gate.

items.title: Anthropic roadshow enters final week — Nov 13 Amodei/Dimon livestream closes the pitch, Nov 18 pricing / Nov 19 trading as ticker 'ANT' on Nasdaq; final week to watch is whether bankers price above the $70-$78 range
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO roadshow entered its final working days before the Nov 18 pricing / Nov 19 trading debut on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ticker 'ANT'. The final public event of the roadshow was a live-streamed conversation between Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, November 13 — framed by coverage as a retail-outreach move tied to the up-to-20% Class A share allocation reserved for retail investors through JPMorgan (US) and Citigroup (international). Market context around the IPO has shifted materially since the Nov 10 S-1/A filing: Bloomberg reported on Nov 11 that the book is 'multiple times oversubscribed' at the filed $70-$78 range, and AI Weekly reported that Nvidia and Google will each anchor approximately $10 billion of the offering, with bankers reportedly discussing a valuation above $1.5 trillion rather than the midpoint of the filed range. A parallel $26 billion private placement from chip and cloud customers is also reportedly running alongside the public float. The retracted pricing email circulated to bankers on Nov 9 (867 million shares at $70-$80, up to ~$69.3 billion in proceeds) has since been superseded by the filed 825 million shares at $70-$78 range, and that distinction now looks like the pre-roadshow version of the deal that was walked back before the roadshow began.
items.why_it_matters: Even for a hobbyist whose exposure to Anthropic is 'I use Claude', the final week of the roadshow is worth paying attention to for three practical reasons that are different from the ones in this morning's am section. First, the pricing outcome on Wednesday evening (Nov 18) will produce a filed data point on what the public market thinks a frontier AI lab is worth — the first such number on record. A price at the top of the filed range ($78) implies a top-of-range valuation around $1.3-1.4 trillion; a price above it would cement the gross-basis accounting method that Anthropic uses as the new default for AI-company valuation discussions, and it would mean the Nvidia + Google anchor positions are the market-moving signal rather than the gross-vs-net accounting debate. A price below $70 is now a tail scenario given the Bloomberg oversubscription report but not impossible. Second, the retail allocation structure Anthropic is using (up to 20% of Class A shares reserved for retail through JPMorgan + Citigroup, plus a CEO livestream as the final roadshow event) is the first major test of the Robinhood-era playbook for a frontier-AI listing. If the retail portion clears cleanly and the stock trades well in the first week, every subsequent AI-lab IPO (OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, Moonshot — which filed in HK yesterday at a $50B valuation) will likely study this structure. Third, the Nov 13 Amodei-Dimon livestream is the kind of event that is historically significant but low-signal in real time — a transcript may not surface for several days, and the content is almost certainly optimized for retail-investor messaging rather than technical substance. The useful thing to extract, if a transcript appears this weekend or early next week, is whatever Amodei says about the unit-economics gap between Anthropic and OpenAI (the $567M Q3 operating loss vs. OpenAI's reported structural deficit), and about the compute commitment structure ($895B in multi-year commitments cited in the S-1/A). Everything else is likely marketing. The one concrete action to consider before Wednesday: if you have a US brokerage account and have been considering direct exposure to Anthropic versus holding it through Amazon or Google, the retail allocation window closes with pricing on Nov 18. After that, you buy in the open market on Nov 19 at whatever the open does.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Anthropic prices Wed Nov 18 as ticker 'ANT' — pricing above the $70-$78 range would cement gross-basis accounting as the new default for AI-lab valuations and validate the Robinhood-era retail-allocation playbook.
